versions.changelog: States the data-flow and credential rules once instead of three times: Privacy & Data Flow is the single authoritative description and the config cheatsheets point at it. Adds a sensitivity note to tracker.py covering the local application log. No control or capability changed.

Removes a stale second manifest: references/SKILL.zh.md carried its own frontmatter declaring license MIT, a git dependency that is never invoked, the superseded env list and the old broad triggers. SKILL.md is now the only manifest. Host-credential opt-in is now per credential (openrouter / telegram_token / telegram_chat). Corrects the docs to say judge.mode=api sends the full JOB_PROFILE.md text, fixes notify_telegram.py's stale docstring, and narrows the README activation example to imperative forms.

Fixes the one 'unexpected' finding from the 1.2.0 scan: credentials are now bound to the endpoint they were issued for, so an OpenRouter key (or the host OpenClaw key) is never forwarded to a custom LLM_BASE_URL and an overridden screen.base_url no longer inherits the judge key. Also narrows activation to imperative triggers, corrects env.example, and clears the static install-source reason code.

Answers the 19 v1.1.0 scan findings: fail-closed per-destination egress consent gate, audible host-credential reads, explicit least-privilege permission declaration, source-discovery disclosure, and correction of three declaration/behaviour mismatches (profile locality, Telegram host-credential reuse, cron write scope) in both the English and Chinese docs.
Security hardening (capability & data-flow disclosure, opt-in host creds, tighter triggers) + stage-1 title screen (progressive scoring, Ollama-friendly) + English-primary docs (Chinese kept)
安全硬化:能力声明+隐私数据流披露+宿主密钥opt-in+收窄触发词

Fix: same-title jobs no longer overwrite each other in KB; retry on truncated HTTP responses; optional JINA_API_KEY. UX: onboarding now asks notification/KB/scraping preferences (with 'all defaults' shortcut) and sends a sample P1 alert after calibration.
Initial release: cron-driven job monitoring engine — LLM-grade matching against your personal profile, application tracking, daily digest. Zero required keys.
